name: Project Documentation Generator
description: An agent that creates project documentation including README files and API docs, and validates the output format for correctness and completeness.

readme-generation.description: Generates well-structured README files with standard sections (title, description, installation, usage, etc.)

tests.description: Generates a README containing all essential sections for a Node.js CLI tool called 'taskflow'
tests.prompt: Generate a README.md for a Node.js CLI tool called 'taskflow' that manages developer tasks via the terminal. It uses SQLite for storage and supports create, list, complete, and delete operations. Install via npm.

tests.description: Output must be valid markdown with proper heading hierarchy
tests.prompt: Generate a README.md for a Python library called 'colorpalette' that extracts dominant colors from images using k-means clustering. It requires Pillow and numpy.

tests.description: README includes code examples in fenced code blocks
tests.prompt: Generate a README.md for a Go HTTP middleware library called 'ratelimit' that provides token-bucket rate limiting. Show how to integrate it with net/http.

api-docs-generation.description: Generates API documentation with endpoints, parameters, request/response examples, and status codes

tests.description: Documents REST API endpoints with methods, paths, and descriptions
tests.prompt: Generate API documentation for a user management REST API with these endpoints: POST /users (create user with name and email), GET /users/:id (get user by ID), PUT /users/:id (update user), DELETE /users/:id (delete user). Include request/response examples.

tests.description: API docs include HTTP status codes for success and error cases
tests.prompt: Generate API documentation for a POST /auth/login endpoint that accepts email and password in JSON body, returns a JWT token on success, and returns errors for invalid credentials and missing fields.

tests.description: API docs contain JSON request/response body examples
tests.prompt: Document a POST /orders endpoint that accepts items (array of {productId, quantity}), shippingAddress (string), and paymentMethod (string). It returns an order object with id, status, total, and createdAt.

tests.description: API docs should not contain TODO placeholders or lorem ipsum filler
tests.prompt: Generate complete API documentation for a GET /products endpoint that returns a paginated list of products with fields: id, name, price, category. Supports query params: page, limit, category.

format-validation.description: Validates that generated documentation follows correct markdown formatting and structural conventions

tests.description: When asked to validate a README, identifies missing standard sections
tests.prompt:
Validate this README and list what's missing:

# MyApp

A cool app.

## Installation

npm install myapp

tests.description: Confirms when documentation has proper structure and completeness
tests.prompt: Validate this README structure: it has Title, Description, Table of Contents, Installation, Usage with code examples, API Reference, Configuration, Contributing, and License sections. All sections contain substantive content. Is this well-structured?

Validate this API doc snippet for correctness:

## GET /health

Returns server health status.

**Response 200:**
```json
{"status": "ok"}
```

contextual-adaptation.description: Adapts documentation style and content to the specific project type, language, and ecosystem conventions

tests.description: Uses Python ecosystem conventions (pip, venv, pyproject.toml) for a Python project
tests.prompt: Generate a README for a Python FastAPI microservice called 'invoice-api' that processes invoices. It uses PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy, and Alembic for migrations.

tests.description: Uses Rust ecosystem conventions (cargo, crates.io) for a Rust project
tests.prompt: Generate a README for a Rust crate called 'blazecache' that provides an in-memory LRU cache with TTL support and async compatibility via tokio.

tests.description: Does not include irrelevant ecosystem tooling when documenting a specific language project
tests.prompt: Generate a README for a pure Go CLI tool called 'logparse' that parses nginx access logs and outputs statistics. No JavaScript, no Python, no Docker — just Go.
